papers.title: How variable and stress-sensitive is sleep expression in lizards?
papers.summary: The study used miniature loggers to measure sleep in wild-caught Peninsular rock agama lizards (Psammophilus dorsalis) from urban and rural environments. Sleep characteristics were largely similar between populations, with urban individuals showing more consolidated daytime sleep bouts and marginally quicker arousal responses at night, while acute restraint stress did not affect sleep.

papers.title: Reading specific memories from human neurons before and after sleep
papers.summary: This study developed a transformer neural network model trained on intracranial neuronal spikes from a single viewing of an audiovisual episode to decode specific concepts during memory recall in individual participants. The model successfully decoded concepts, and analysis revealed distinct contributions from medial temporal lobe and frontal cortex before and after sleep, suggesting a shift in neural information distribution across wake/sleep cycles.

papers.title: A Dynamic Model of Weekly Sleep Timing: Endogenous Origins of Social Jetlag.
papers.summary: The authors developed a dynamic model integrating the two-process model of sleep regulation with time-allocation decisions, showing that weekly sleep patterns including social jetlag can emerge endogenously from behavioral tradeoffs over scarce workday leisure, without requiring fixed wake times or bedtimes. The model reproduces shorter workday sleep, weekend recovery sleep, and later free-day midsleep, and brings simulated patterns closer to empirical estimates when realistic constraints are added.

papers.title: The effects of deep TMS on QEEG power, asymmetry, and coherence metrics in major depressive disorder.
papers.summary: This study examined the effects of deep transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) on quantitative EEG (QEEG) measures in 75 patients with major depressive disorder. After a 36-session protocol, depressive symptoms significantly reduced (82.6% response rate), along with decreased delta activity in the left prefrontal cortex, leftward frontal beta asymmetry shift, and improved coherence between left prefrontal and temporal lobes.

papers.title: Circadian misalignment in healthy young adults influences the variability of inhibitory performance modeled by the horse race model.
papers.summary: This study examined the association between social jetlag and inhibitory control in healthy young adults using the horse-race model. Higher social jetlag predicted longer stop-signal reaction times and greater race model values, indicating delayed inhibition processes, while raw reaction times showed no significant association, highlighting the value of computational modeling.

papers.title: Resting-State Functional Connectivity Alterations in Insomnia Disorder: A Systematic Review of Studies Published from 2020 to July 2025.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized resting-state functional connectivity (rsFC) studies in insomnia disorder published from 2020 to July 2025. It found alterations in multiple brain networks and sleep-wake hubs compatible with hyperarousal, but methodological heterogeneity precluded quantitative pooling, and cross-sectional designs limit causal inference.

papers.title: Exploratory definition of a clinically meaningful change in intracranial EEG features: Analysis of data from a long-term treatment study of the RNS® System.
papers.summary: This post hoc analysis of data from a long-term RNS System treatment study in patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy sought to define a clinically meaningful change in intracranial EEG long episode (LE) frequency. A LE reduction of ≥30% was associated with a ≥50% clinical seizure reduction (AUC=0.765), supporting LE reduction as a potential biomarker.

papers.title: Agreement between smartphone-based mobile sensing and actigraphy sleep metrics in young people with bipolar disorder.
papers.summary: This study compared smartphone-based mobile sensing with actigraphy for sleep metrics in youth with bipolar disorder, finding strong agreement for sleep timing and duration, with the strongest agreement for midsleep (RMSE = 14.8 minutes). Mobile sensing slightly overestimated sleep duration and underestimated wake after sleep onset, but was sensitive to the presence of nocturnal wakefulness, supporting its potential for scalable monitoring.

papers.title: Stage-Specific Effects of Maternal Circadian Rhythm Disruption during Pre-Pregnancy, Pregnancy, and Lactation on Behavioral and Neurobiological Outcomes in Male Rat Offspring.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of maternal circadian rhythm disruption during distinct reproductive stages (pre-pregnancy, pregnancy, lactation) on male rat offspring. Offspring from pre-pregnancy and pregnancy disruption showed increased anxiety- and depressive-like behaviors, altered hippocampal CA1 morphology, and molecular changes, while lactation disruption had fewer effects, suggesting stage-specific impacts on neurodevelopment.

papers.title: Multimodal assessment of sleep and regional brain volumes in AQP4-IgG-positive neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder: An exploratory cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This exploratory cross-sectional study assessed sleep and brain volumes in AQP4-IgG-positive NMOSD, finding longer time in bed and total sleep time by actigraphy, no differences in sleep efficiency or wake after sleep onset, and worse subjective sleep disturbance. Volume reductions were seen in hippocampal subfields and corpus callosum segments, but no volume-sleep associations survived correction.

papers.title: Circadian and behavioral timing in MASLD: a systematic review of human observational studies.
papers.summary: This systematic review of 24 human observational studies found that shift work showed the most consistent associations with MASLD, while chronotype, sleep timing, and other circadian exposures had less consistent or limited evidence. Heterogeneity and confounding preclude causal conclusions, and prospective studies with objective circadian phenotyping are needed.

papers.title: Differential modulation of sensorimotor alpha rhythms by motor imagery, electrical stimulation, and mirror visual feedback following peripheral nerve reconstruction: an EEG study.
papers.summary: This EEG study compared sensorimotor alpha rhythm modulation during motor imagery, electrical stimulation, and mirror visual feedback in 11 patients after peripheral nerve reconstruction and 21 healthy controls. Patients showed significant alpha suppression during electrical stimulation and mirror visual feedback, but not during motor imagery alone, suggesting multimodal rehabilitation may better facilitate cortical reorganization.

papers.title: Amyloid beta plaque pathology induces chemosensory deficits and increases apnoeas in the 5XFAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: In 5XFAD mice, amyloid beta plaque deposition in brainstem respiratory regions was associated with increased spontaneous apnoeas and blunted hypoxic and hypercapnic ventilatory responses, indicating chemosensory dysfunction. This suggests a link between Aβ pathology and respiratory deficits in Alzheimer's disease models.

papers.title: Sleep fragmentation and heightened inflammation: A latent profile subtype predicting nine-year major depressive disorder severity in the MIDUS study.
papers.summary: Using latent profile analysis in 306 adults, a profile characterized by high inflammation and sleep disturbances predicted 9-year major depressive disorder severity beyond baseline. This suggests that a person-centered neuroimmune profile may serve as a distal risk factor for depression.

papers.title: Brain dynamic audio stimulation for subjective sleep disturbances in healthcare professionals: a single-arm pilot feasibility study.
papers.summary: This pilot feasibility study tested a 14-day Brain Dynamic Audio Stimulation (BDAS) intervention in healthcare professionals with subjective sleep disturbances. Results showed high retention and significant reductions in insomnia severity scores and sleep onset latency, with EEG changes suggesting improved sleep initiation.

papers.title: Association of Obstructive Sleep Apnoea Severity with Nocturnal Blood Pressure and Autonomic Dysfunction in Patients with Hypertension.
papers.journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
papers.summary: An observational study of hypertensive patients found that greater obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, measured by AHI, was associated with higher nocturnal systolic blood pressure after adjustment, with trends toward reduced nocturnal blood pressure dipping and altered autonomic function.

papers.title: Psilocybin-induced changes in electroencephalography link acute and long-term effects.
papers.summary: In a double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with 20 healthy participants, psilocybin acutely reduced alpha/beta EEG power and increased gamma-band signal diversity, which correlated with acute psychological effects; at 24 hours, reduced delta/theta power correlated with positive life changes at 4 weeks, suggesting a sub-acute 'afterglow' distinct from acute psychological intensity.

papers.title: Longitudinal associations between emotional eating and sleep disturbances: A Generation R study.
papers.summary: In 3216 Generation R adolescents, no overall within-person cross-lagged associations between emotional eating and sleep disturbances were found, but concurrent co-occurrence was observed at age 18. Subgroup analyses showed that emotional eating at age 14 predicted sleep disturbances at age 18 in European-origin and low-overweight-risk youth.

papers.title: Microstructural Brain Reserve Moderates the Associations Between 24-h Movement Behaviors and Cognition in Older Adults: Cross-Sectional Findings From the AGUEDA Trial.
papers.journal: Scandinavian journal of medicine & science in sports
papers.summary: Cross-sectional analysis from the AGUEDA trial found no direct associations between 24-hour movement behaviors and cognition in older adults, but gray matter mean diffusivity (GMMD) moderated associations, particularly for episodic memory and light physical activity, indicating the importance of microstructural brain integrity.

papers.title: A U-shaped relationship between perceived chronic stress and the approach motivation: evidence from resting-state EEG.
papers.summary: In 60 undergraduates, perceived chronic stress showed a U-shaped relationship with resting-state EEG measures of approach motivation, including alpha frontal asymmetry and delta/theta power. This nonlinear pattern suggests that both low and high stress enhance baseline approach motivation, while moderate stress reduces it.

papers.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Combined With Electroencephalography Analysis Suggest Time-Dependent and Region-Specific Modulation of Cortical Excitability During Acute Alcohol Intoxication.
papers.summary: In 34 healthy adults, acute alcohol intoxication decreased TMS-evoked EEG potential amplitudes (P30, N45, P60, N100, P180) and global mean field power in a time-dependent and region-specific manner, with effects most prominent in frontal and central regions, indicating dynamic modulation of cortical excitability.

papers.title: Improving career guidance accuracy through EEG-based vocational interest assessment and self-reported RIASEC profiles.
papers.summary: This study compared EEG-based vocational interest assessments with self-reported RIASEC profiles in 33 participants, finding strong overall convergence but discrepancies that led to different occupational recommendations, suggesting neurometrics can complement self-report measures.

papers.title: Influence of Guideline-Based Carbohydrate Intake on Training Adaptations, Health, and Sleep in Female Rugby Athletes: An Exploratory Study.
papers.journal: International journal of sport nutrition and exercise metabolism
papers.summary: This exploratory study investigated the effects of higher (6 g/kg/d) versus lower (3 g/kg/d) carbohydrate intake on training adaptations, health, and sleep in female rugby athletes over a 7-week preseason. Despite increasing energy availability, the intervention did not significantly alter training adaptations, physique, or biochemical markers, but reduced sleep duration on training nights.

papers.title: Heart Rate Variability During Short-Term Electroencephalography.
papers.summary: The study measured heart rate variability (HRV) in 103 patients undergoing routine short-term EEG and found reduced HRV compared to normal values, indicating that a normal EEG does not predict normal HRV. HRV was stable across wakefulness and sleep stages, suggesting that measuring HRV during the first five minutes of EEG could provide useful prognostic information.

papers.title: Application of numerical simulation of upper airway flow field in pediatric obstructive sleep apnea with adenoid hypertrophy.
papers.journal: Quantitative imaging in medicine and surgery
papers.summary: Computational fluid dynamics simulations of the upper airway in children with adenoid hypertrophy showed that AH significantly reduced nasopharyngeal cross-sectional area, increasing pressure, flow velocity, and wall shear stress, while adenoidectomy restored airflow parameters to near-normal levels.

papers.title: Effect of multidimensional perioperative factors on postoperative delayed neurocognitive recovery in elderly patients undergoing single-port video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy: A prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 309 elderly patients undergoing single-port VATS lobectomy identified multidimensional perioperative predictors of delayed neurocognitive recovery (DNR). Higher Surgical Apgar Score was protective, while higher Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale scores were independent risk factors, with an AUC of 0.919.

papers.title: Association of Sleep Duration, Metabolic Markers, and Risk of All-Cause and Cause-Specific Mortality in China and the UK.
papers.summary: Using data from the China Kadoorie Biobank and UK Biobank, this study examined associations between sleep duration, metabolic markers, and mortality. It found that sleep duration was associated with specific lipid metabolites (e.g., lipoprotein subclasses, ketone bodies) which were also linked to all-cause and cause-specific mortality, suggesting a mediating role of lipid metabolism.

papers.title: Epilepsy Is Part of the CNS Phenotype in Classic Infantile Pompe Disease.
authors: Johanna M P Van Den Hout
papers.summary: This international retrospective study of 17 patients with classic infantile Pompe disease found that epilepsy is part of the CNS phenotype, with seizures occurring predominantly after age 7 years. Most patients had EEG abnormalities, cognitive impairment, white matter changes, and elevated serum neurofilament light chain, and 70% became seizure-free on antiseizure medication.

papers.title: Alamandine Attenuates Hypoxia-Induced Atrial Fibrillation in Rats: Involvement of Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress and Pyroptosis Pathways.
papers.summary: This study examined the effect of alamandine on atrial fibrillation induced by chronic intermittent hypoxia in rats. Alamandine reduced atrial fibrillation susceptibility and attenuated endoplasmic reticulum stress and pyroptosis-related protein expression, suggesting its potential as a therapeutic agent for AF.

papers.title: Respiratory Support With Nasal High Flow Reduces Opioid Requirements During Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography.
papers.summary: In this open-label randomized controlled trial, 94 patients undergoing ERCP under dexmedetomidine-based sedation were randomized to nasal high flow (NHF) or low-flow oxygen. NHF significantly reduced opioid requirements (median pethidine dose 43.75 mg vs. 70.00 mg) while maintaining oxygenation and ventilation.

papers.title: Over-hydration as a key modifiable predictor of obstructive sleep apnea severity in dialysis patients with daytime sleepiness.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 40 dialysis patients with excessive daytime sleepiness found that over-hydration, assessed by body composition monitoring, was an independent predictor of obstructive sleep apnea severity, particularly in peritoneal dialysis patients. The Epworth Sleepiness Scale was suggested as a useful screening tool.

papers.title: Combination of stereo-electroencephalography and electrocorticography to manage mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE): a case report.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes a 25-year-old patient with mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy (MOGHE) in the right temporal lobe, who had a delayed diagnosis and extensive epileptogenic areas. After surgical resection of the right temporal and frontal regions, the patient experienced only occasional minor focal seizures over 14 months, suggesting that larger resection may improve outcomes in delayed MOGHE cases.

papers.title: Models for identifying cognitive frailty in hospitalized older adults with chronic heart failure in China: a systematic review.
papers.summary: This systematic review evaluated models for identifying cognitive frailty in hospitalized older adults with chronic heart failure in China, finding eight cross-sectional studies with 20 models, all at high risk of bias. The models were diagnostic for prevalent cognitive frailty rather than prognostic, with limited external validation and none ready for clinical use.

papers.title: Latent profiles of workplace violence exposure and predictive modeling of sleep disorders among emergency department nurses: A nationwide cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1540 Chinese emergency department nurses used latent profile analysis to identify three workplace violence exposure patterns (low-level, moderate multi-form, high multi-form) and machine learning to predict sleep disorders, which affected 59.3% of participants. Random forest achieved the highest predictive performance (AUC=0.624), with burnout and occupational characteristics contributing more to predictions than violence profiles.

papers.title: Predictivity of preoperative weight loss on co-morbidity resolution in bariatric patients.
papers.journal: Surgery for obesity and related diseases : official journal of the American Society for Bariatric Surgery
papers.summary: This retrospective study of 788 bariatric surgery patients found that preoperative percent of excess weight loss was significantly associated with resolution of diabetes and hyperlipidemia during the immediate postoperative period (1-6 months). At 1 year, diabetes resolution was highest at 80.0%, followed by hypertension (61.1%), hyperlipidemia (53.3%), and obstructive sleep apnea (29.3%).

papers.title: Successful treatment with teduglutide in short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure secondary to small-bowel volvulus: a case report and literature review.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
papers.summary: The paper reports a case of a 70-year-old man with short bowel syndrome with intestinal failure after small-bowel volvulus, treated with teduglutide. Treatment led to complete weaning from parenteral nutrition, improved stool consistency and frequency, resolution of catheter-related bloodstream infections, and improved quality of life.

papers.title: Routine metabolic and nutrition-related composite indices for identifying adverse cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic phenotypes: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 1,226 adults undergoing routine health examinations found that adverse cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) phenotype (stage >=2) was present in 58.56% of participants. The atherogenic index of plasma (AIP) and triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index showed high discrimination (AUC 0.87) for prevalent adverse CKM phenotype, with random forest achieving the best internal performance (AUC 0.89).

papers.title: Giant esophageal schwannoma mimicking a mediastinal tumor: a case report and review of the literature.
papers.journal: International journal of surgery case reports
papers.summary: This case report describes a 55-year-old man with a giant benign esophageal schwannoma mimicking a mediastinal tumor, which was resected via subtotal esophagectomy with retrosternal gastric tube reconstruction. The tumor showed high FDG uptake on PET despite benign pathology, highlighting diagnostic challenges; the patient remained recurrence-free at 1 year postoperatively.

papers.title: Comparative Evaluation of the Efficacy, Safety, and Corneal Dynamics of Overnight Orthokeratology in Teenagers and Adults With Myopia: A Prospective, Open-Label Study in Taiwan.
papers.summary: This prospective study in Taiwan compared overnight orthokeratology in 15 teenagers and 53 adults with myopia over 9 months. Both groups achieved significant improvement in uncorrected visual acuity to approximately 20/20 and reduction of spherical equivalent to about 0.0 D, with minimal corneal staining and stable endothelial cell density, and returned to baseline by week 4 after discontinuation.

papers.title: Letter to the Editor Regarding "Effect of Remimazolam Versus Propofol Sedation on Postoperative Sleep Quality Following Gastroscopy: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study" [Response to Letter].
papers.summary: This document is a response to a letter regarding a study on remimazolam versus propofol sedation and postoperative sleep quality after gastroscopy. It addresses comments about the original study.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
